Subject: RFI: TAM retainer coverage details and escalation timelines

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick intro call this week. As part of our RFI we need a detailed breakdown of what a TAM retainer with Redwood would include operationally. Specifically:

- Standard support hours (local and global) and guaranteed response/acknowledgement SLAs by severity
- On-call rotation (who triages, handoff cadence) and whether escalation to engineering is included
- Typical incident timeline examples (acknowledge -> triage -> workaround -> fix) with realistic target windows
- Communication plan for P1/P2 incidents including frequency of updates and channel (phone, Slack, email)

We're on a tight timeline — can you send a detailed RFI response and any supporting artifacts (schedule matrix, contact pdf, example runbook snippets) by EOD next Wednesday 10/18?

Hi Lisa,

Thanks — we can absolutely provide that. I've attached a preliminary coverage schedule and the escalation contacts PDF for your review. High-level answers below; we'll follow up with the full packet by 10/18 EOD as requested.

- Support hours & SLAs: Tiered model. Business-hours (Mon-Fri 6am-6pm PT) included in retainer with 4-hour acknowledge for Sev 1 / 8-hour for Sev 2. Extended coverage (24x7 monitoring & on-call triage) is an add-on included for P1s in most enterprise plans.
- On-call rotation: TAM-led triage during business hours; 24x7 pager rotation handled by our Incident Response pool when purchased. Handoff cadence: daily shift notes + weekly sync.
- Escalation: TAM -> Support Escalation Engineer -> On-call Engineering (if needed). We include one engineering escalation per quarter in retainer; additional engineering deep dives billed per-incident or covered under a separate eng-retainer.
- Incident comms: P1 updates every 30 minutes until mitigation, P2 every 4 hours. Channels: vendor phone bridge, Slack channel (private customer workspace), and written incident digest post-mitigation.

Internal: @Grace, @Karthik — please review the attached Draft_TAM_Retainer_SLA and the Support_Coverage_Schedule. Any changes to the ack windows or escalation allowances before I send the consolidated response to FinBank?

Thanks Tessa. Quick bullets from product/TAM ops side:

- 24x7 pager triage: we can include initial triage (ack + initial mitigation attempt) for P1s in the enterprise retainer. Rule of thumb: first ack within 30 minutes, initial triage within 2 hours.
- Engineering escalation: include one named engineering deep-dive per quarter; emergency engineering escalation available 24x7 but billed separately unless covered by eng-retainer.
- Handoff & runbook: daily shift handoffs captured in our incident log; we will include a sanitized runbook excerpt that shows triage steps and communication templates.
- Sample incident timeline (typical):
  * 00:00 — Pager fires, TAM ack (<=30m)
  * 00:45 — Initial triage, collect logs & KV cache snapshot
  * 02:30 — Workaround deployed (if applicable)
  * 08:00 — Engineering fix rollout begins (if root cause requires code change)
  * Post-incident — 72h RCA window for delivery of full analysis

Neha — on roster cadence: we typically run 7-day rotations for TAM ops with 48-hour hand-off overlap between shifts. Is that still feasible with current headcount?

I will add the sanitized runbook snippet to the Draft_TAM_Retainer_SLA and tighten the wording on SLAs.

— Grace
